solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very large intelligence service for East German citizens

parts.note: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize
the Secret Intelligence Service, Britain's foreign spy agency

explanation.surface: A huge Stasi-like spy agency set up to watch the people of the old GDR.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossi is the German colloquial nickname for a person from the former East Germany; the plural is the answer.

clue.text: Jaguars seen in parts of pound

definitions.meaning: first meaning: big wild cats, a sense Chambers gives for this word
second meaning: sixteenths of a pound weight

explanation.surface: Jaguar cars spotted in sections of a dog pound or a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The usual ounce is the snow leopard, but Chambers allows the name for other wild cats, the jaguar among them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a sixteenth of an avoirdupois pound, and also a name for several large spotted cats.

clue.text: One is able to get below splinter, thin wooden strip

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting below puts the able-one pieces underneath the splinter word

parts.note: a spell is a dialect word for a splinter of wood

explanation.surface: Someone manages to work a splinter loose from under a strip of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'get below' places the 'one is able' part under the splinter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Spillikins (spellicans) are the thin slips of wood used in the game of jackstraws.

clue.text: Henry finally cracked latest secret procedure

indicators.note: finally tells us the Henry abbreviation is placed at the very end
something cracked is broken apart, so the following word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Henry at last breaks the newest covert method.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is acting furtively, a covert way of proceeding so as not to be noticed.

clue.text: Joins up for respect as before

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: joins, as roads or people meet

explanation.surface: Someone enlists in search of esteem, as in the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Steem is the obsolete form of esteem, so 'as before' marks it as archaic respect.

clue.text: Hearts sit back in Inverness ground — that's trouble in Edinburgh

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the gathered letters are mixed

parts.note: H is the card abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: in says the letter comes from inside the place name that follows

parts.note: the final letter of the Highland town
surface padding in this reading; the blog instead reverses the first two pieces

explanation.surface: Hearts fans sit back at an Inverness ground, and there is trouble in Edinburgh.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose wordplay: the blog also reads it as the reversal of 'Hearts sit' inside S...IE. Hearts (Heart of Midlothian) is an Edinburgh football club, which is the surface's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Stishie (stushie) is a Scots word for a commotion or row, the kind of fuss heard in Scotland's capital.

clue.text: Swallow almost over meadow looks up for a kestrel

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to swallow an insult is to stand it, tolerate it

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading the word from the bottom upward

parts.note: a ley is grassland or meadow

explanation.surface: A swallow nearly passes over a field and a kestrel glances upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird, sitting nicely beside a kestrel, but it is the verb meaning tolerate. 'Over' places the first part above the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanyel (staniel) is an old dialect name for the kestrel, a small falcon.

clue.text: Bit of trouble with slightly indecent lady

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

explanation.surface: A little bother involving a rather saucy woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracy is a woman's first name, and crosswords freely define such names by 'lady' or 'girl'.

clue.text: Quiet member of secret US fraternity for friendly chat

parts.note: a member of the Loyal Order of Moose, an American fraternal society

explanation.surface: A discreet member of an American secret society, out for a cosy talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Shmoose (schmooze) is Yiddish-derived slang for gossiping or chatting in a friendly, ingratiating way.

clue.text: What's up with flipping endless junk mail? Very much

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the short question word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eh is a request to repeat what was said

indicators.note: flipping turns the mail word over so it reads backwards
endless means the last letter of the mail word is removed

explanation.surface: Annoyed at all the blasted spam, someone asks what's going on: there's loads of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' poses as a mild British expletive but reverses the junk mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaps is informal for a great deal, as in 'thanks heaps'.

clue.text: The Crown dropped very harmful alcohol

indicators.note: the crown of a down entry is its top, so the first letter is taken away

explanation.surface: The monarchy abandoned a dangerously potent drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Crown' reads as the monarchy, but it means the head of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethal is cetyl alcohol, a waxy chemical alcohol obtained from spermaceti.

clue.text: Lawyer's briefly right behind drawing

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short to its abbreviation

parts.note: Att. is a short form of attorney

explanation.surface: A lawyer's quick sketch is right at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests a picture, but it is an adjective: pulling toward.
explanation.definitionFit: Attrahent means attracting or pulling in, as a muscle or a magnet draws something toward it.

clue.text: Diamond mentioned for a pointer once

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the singer's first name

explanation.surface: A diamond referred to as an old-fashioned indicator, perhaps on a gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diamond' suggests a gem or a card suit; it is the singer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Neele is an obsolete spelling of needle, the pointer of a compass or dial.

clue.text: One jolly good hour to go round anonymous town

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the earlier letters enclose the next

parts.note: a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A really fun hour spent touring some nameless town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly good' reads as one phrase, but jolly is a Royal Marine and good is just G; RM and G go round the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagh is a cathedral city and county town in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Enclosure in county for four-wheeled carriage

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

parts.note: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland
enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure on letters

explanation.surface: A paddock in the shires made over for a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarence is a closed four-wheeled horse carriage, named after the Duke of Clarence.

clue.text: Spouts about university protest? That's the wordplay!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the spouting word surrounds the others

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: Someone rants about a campus protest, and the punchline is a pun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' links the wordplay to the definition, which wittily names the crossword's own stock in trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeu de mots is French for a pun, a play on words.

clue.text: Girl's lines penned by river

indicators.note: penned by means shut in by, so the river word encloses the lines

parts.note: ea is a dialect word for a river
L is line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A young woman's verses were written beside a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella is a female first name, which crosswords define simply as 'girl'.

clue.text: Months to get case of ecological wine

parts.note: mos is the abbreviation for months

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only the outer letters are kept

explanation.surface: It takes months to obtain a crate of organic wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' sounds like a case of wine, apt beside the definition, but it means the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosel is the German white wine from the Moselle valley.

clue.text: Extinct reptile goes astray in lax USA? Right

indicators.note: in places the first jumble inside the second
going astray means wandering off course, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: rt is an abbreviation for right

indicators.note: something lax is loose, so the country's letters plus the right abbreviation are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dinosaur wanders loose in a permissive America; is that right?
explanation.definitionFit: A stegosaur is a plated herbivorous dinosaur of the Jurassic, long extinct.

clue.text: Pass on advice for putting out dip

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an instruction to extinguish a dip, a cheap candle

explanation.surface: Pass along a tip on getting rid of a dip, like a party snack.
explanation.walkthrough: A dip is a candle made by dipping a wick in tallow; the slang for dying is literally an order to put one out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for dying, and read literally tells someone to extinguish a candle.

clue.text: With a change of direction, young women become hunting guides

indicators.note: a change of direction swaps one direction letter for the other, right for left

explanation.surface: Girls who change course turn into guides for shooting parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Gillies are Scottish attendants who guide those out hunting, stalking or fishing.

clue.text: Short match covered in one language

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped inside, so the match goes inside the word for one

parts.note: a vesta is a short wax match

explanation.surface: A brief contest wrapped up in a single tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short match' suggests a quick game; a vesta is a short match for lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Avestan is the ancient Iranian language of the Zoroastrian scriptures, the Avesta.

clue.text: Fossilized footprint possibly neolithic

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A footprint preserved in stone, maybe from the New Stone Age.
explanation.definitionFit: An ichnolite is a stone bearing the fossil track of an animal, from Greek ichnos, track.

clue.text: Peevish All Blacks briefly involved in brawl

indicators.note: involved in means caught up inside, so the team abbreviation goes within the brawl word
briefly says the team name is cut to its short form

parts.note: the All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby team

explanation.surface: Irritable rugby players caught up in a punch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Franzy is a dialect word for fretful or irritable.

clue.text: Huge sea wave from the east, those on edge off to get a hand

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left
the letters on the edges are removed, leaving only the inner ones

parts.note: a tsunami is a giant sea wave

explanation.surface: A giant wave rolls in from the east, and anyone nervous wants a helping hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge' looks like nervousness, but it means the end letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Manus is the Latin and anatomical term for the hand.

clue.text: Brazilian racer seen in Tuscan town

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Felipe ..., the Formula One driver
second meaning: the provincial capital in north-west Tuscany

explanation.surface: A Brazilian racing driver spotted in an Italian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Felipe Massa drove for Ferrari, and Massa is also a town near Carrara in Tuscany.

clue.text: Term for stubborn fellow supporting nothing?

definitions.text: Term for stubborn fellow supporting nothing?

indicators.note: a term is an end, so the last letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A name for an obstinate person who backs nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts the fellow below the earlier letters. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-man is one who habitually refuses or says no, the opposite of a yes-man.

clue.text: Sow's first once was called a slip

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the pig word is used

parts.note: hote is an archaic past tense of hight, to be called

explanation.surface: The sow's firstborn used to be known as a runt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' suggests an error, but it is a young pig, which suits the sow.
explanation.definitionFit: A shote is a young weaned pig, and slip is a dialect word for a young pig too.

clue.text: See less hard frosty periods in Shetland seed times

indicators.note: less means minus, and the letter for hard is removed

parts.note: v. is vide, Latin for see
hoars are spells of hoar frost

explanation.surface: Look at milder frosty spells during the planting season in the Shetland Isles.
explanation.definitionFit: Voar is the Orkney and Shetland word for spring, the season for sowing.

clue.text: Not so many leaving with old mate

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for with goes away

parts.note: w is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Fewer people head off together with an old friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Feer (fere) is an archaic word for a companion or spouse.

clue.text: Child that's tiny, also mistreated — mother expecting complaint

indicators.note: something tiny is cut down, so the word is shortened to its abbreviation

parts.note: ch. is an abbreviation for child

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A small child is badly treated too, while the mother is pregnant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother expecting' reads as one phrase, but mother gives the last two letters and 'expecting complaint' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloasma is brownish skin pigmentation, notably the 'mask of pregnancy' affecting women expecting a baby.

clue.text: No tips for unchanging fare in Chinese outfit

indicators.note: the tips are the end letters, and no tips means they are cut off

parts.note: fare, as in what is served

explanation.surface: No gratuities for the monotonous food served in a Chinese restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No tips' reads as no gratuities for the waiter; here it removes the final letter of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A samfoo is a Chinese woman's costume of a jacket worn over trousers.

clue.text: This guy is merciless, leaving wife

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for wife departs from the word

explanation.surface: A man is so pitiless that his wife walks out on him.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton is a man's first name, so it can be referred to as a guy.

clue.text: Slops put out in litres, say

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Dirty liquid poured out by the litre, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it supplies three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaistery is a Scots word for messy slops or sloppy refuse.

clue.text: Relations free from restraint in all sections

indicators.note: in places the freeing word inside the selected letters
sections suggests taking a piece of each word, here the opening one

explanation.surface: Family members released from all restrictions, everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of 'all sections' wrap round the verb meaning release.
explanation.definitionFit: Aunts are relatives, and aunties is the familiar plural.

clue.text: Society noisy about wanting independence, plump for Sturgeon

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the remaining letters are rearranged
wanting means lacking, so the letter for independence is removed

explanation.surface: A rowdy society, minus independence, backs Nicola Sturgeon, the former Scottish First Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plump for' looks like choosing, but plump is the adjective, and 'for Sturgeon' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonsy is Scots for buxom or plump and comely, a word Sturgeon as a Scot would use.
